models.title: Herfindahl-Hirschman concentration index
models.summary: Concentration as the sum of squared constituent weights.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM1 Benchmark Selection, printed p. 32 (PDF p. 42), Equation 1; Exhibit 12 sums to 0.03889
relationship.translation_notes: Family W holds the precomputed squared weights w_i² (squaring documented here as the per-element construction; no elementwise family arithmetic exists in the grammar, so elements are bound as squared values). Decimal weights (unit 1); the 0–10,000 antitrust scale is the same sum over percentage weights and is not mixed in. Dimensional check: dimensionless sum.

variables.source_symbol: w_i² per constituent (introduced family of squared weights)
variables.definition: Squared portfolio weight of each constituent, in decimal-weight units
variables.context: same fully invested long-only portfolio at one measurement date
variables.domain: Closed interval 0 to 1 per element; elements jointly consistent with weights summing to 1

variables.definition: Herfindahl-Hirschman concentration index on the decimal-weight scale (1/n for equal weights, 1.0 for a single holding)
variables.context: same fully invested long-only portfolio at one measurement date

assumptions: Fully invested long-only weights summing to 1;decimal-weight scale (percentage-scale HHIs must be divided by 10,000 first, per corroborating source).
limitations: Weight-based concentration only; ignores correlations, sectors, volatility and liquidity (per corroborating source).
Family size capped at 256 elements; broader indexes must be pre-aggregated.
Antitrust application uses market shares of firms rather than portfolio weights; same arithmetic, different context.

sources.redistribution: Short original paraphrase and single-formula transcription only; no extended quotation

references.provenance: Published result: LM1 Exhibit 12, printed p. 33 (PDF p. 43)

references.method: Source's reported NASDAQ 100 squared-weight total 0.0404, entered as its two published group subtotals (top-five 0.38² concentrated portion 0.04 plus remainder 0.0004); sum reproduces the published total.

models.title: Effective number of stocks from concentration
models.summary: Equal-weight-equivalent holding count as the reciprocal of the concentration index.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM1 Benchmark Selection, printed p. 32 (PDF p. 42), Equation 2; 1/0.03889 = 25.71 and 1/0.0404 = 24.75
relationship.translation_notes: Decimal-weight HHI only; a 0–10,000-scale HHI converts as 10,000/HHI (per corroborating source). Result is a unitless equivalent count, need not be whole. Dimensional check: dimensionless reciprocal.

variables.definition: Herfindahl-Hirschman index on the decimal-weight scale (same meaning as HHI record output)
variables.context: same fully invested long-only portfolio at one measurement date

variables.definition: Number of equal-weighted holdings with the same weight-based concentration
variables.context: same fully invested long-only portfolio at one measurement date

assumptions: Fully invested long-only portfolio; decimal-weight HHI scale.
limitations: Equivalent-count interpretation only; actual holding count and diversification benefit differ (per source: 100 stocks ≡ ~25 equal-weighted).
Not a count of independent risk sources; ignores correlations.

models.title: Bond current yield
models.summary: Annual coupon income per unit of current bond price.

relationship.original_equation: Coupon income (or Current yield) = Annual coupon payment/Current bond price
relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 Decomposing Expected Returns, printed p. 66 (PDF p. 76); £2.75/£97.12 = 2.83% and $3.63/$117.00 = 3.10%
relationship.translation_notes: Assumes no reinvestment income (per source). Decimal form: 2.83% as 0.0283. Yield-income component of rolling yield (separate record). Dimensional check: currency / currency = dimensionless yield.

variables.definition: Bond's annual coupon payment, in currency units
variables.context: same bond and price date as price

variables.definition: Bond's current market (clean) price, in the same currency units as coupon
variables.context: same bond and price date as coupon

variables.definition: Current yield: annual income per unit of price, in decimal form
variables.context: same bond and price date as inputs

assumptions: No reinvestment income included (per source); accrued interest conventions follow the quoted clean price.
limitations: Income-only snapshot: ignores pull-to-par, reinvestment and price changes (per corroborating source's shortcomings section).
Zero-coupon bonds have zero current yield by construction.

models.title: Bond rolldown return
models.summary: Percentage price change from aging along an unchanged yield curve.

relationship.original_equation: Rolldown return = (Bond price end-of-horizon − Bond price beginning-of-horizon)/Bond price beginning-of-horizon
relationship.translation_notes: Unchanged-curve isolation: revalue the aged bond at the horizon on the starting curve; coupon income stays separate (rolling-yield record). Decimal form. Dimensional check: currency difference / currency = dimensionless return.

variables.definition: Bond price at the start of the horizon, in currency units
variables.context: same bond, unchanged yield curve, one horizon period

variables.definition: Revalued bond price at the horizon (aged, same curve), in the same currency units
variables.context: same bond, unchanged yield curve, one horizon period

variables.definition: Rolldown return over the horizon from curve-aging only, in decimal form (signed; negative toward higher-yield points)
variables.context: same bond, unchanged yield curve, one horizon period

assumptions: Yield curve unchanged over the horizon; zero interest-rate volatility in the revaluation (per source).
Prices are same-convention (both clean or both dirty) at the two dates.
limitations: Isolates the aging effect only; realized return also reflects coupon, curve shifts, spread and currency changes.
Premium bonds show losses and discount bonds gains toward par even on a flat curve (pull-to-par).
First-order duration approximation (−ModDur × Δyield) is an alternative route, not this record's definition.

models.title: Bond rolling yield
models.summary: Static-curve expected yield as coupon income plus rolldown return.

relationship.original_equation: Rolling yield = Coupon income + Rolldown return
relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 Rolldown Return, printed p. 67 (PDF p. 77); 2.83% + 0.17% = 3.00% and solutions 3.10% − 2.56% = 0.54%
relationship.translation_notes: Both inputs in decimal form (unit 1). Named static-curve combination; excludes benchmark-yield, spread and currency views (separate E(R) components). Dimensional check: dimensionless + dimensionless = dimensionless yield.
